title: Tio's lessons: duets and figuring out music
summary: Gorman recounts Tio's duets with pupils and his view of working out music like counting money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did he ever play his instrument at the lessons or what did he do? Just listen or did he have his clarinet too?

Well, I tell you what you do. As long as you was going along, all right, he let you go. You understand what I mean? Now, now and then him and I used to make duets together. He said, well, all right, you're doing fine. Now let's take this duet tonight. He said, now what line you want to take? The top line or the bottom line? Now you suggest this, what line? If you want him to play the bottom, you play the bottom. If you want him to play the top, you play the top. And sometimes you play the bottom, you say, well, all right, now you take the top. I'm going to play the bottom. Now, you made a mistake. You make it like this. Then you take his own and make it. That's the kind of man he is. But when he learned you something, you had it. And he'll never take you off the lesson, no lesson you have the understanding. Now this is something else he explained to me. Many times I used to sit down and think about, if a man is trying to figure out a piece of music, some people figure you take a horn, your instrument. Like you play a clarinet, you figure out the instruments. You know, I mean you take your horn and figure out that, I mean your instruments, you know what I mean? But you see you don't work it that way. When you figure out a piece of music it's just like you figure out a piece of, I mean money. It's all in you. Now you have to know how to count that. You know how to add, you know how to take off this fellow and put it a little bit on that. Well that's why a lot of fellas tell you a musician is a thief. Well I believe it in the way of speaking because sometimes he steals from one note and put it on the other one. Is that right? Yeah, that's right. You've got to do that, you understand what I mean? Well, now this professor used to tell me that all the time.
